title: Fractions as lengths check-in

pretest.q: A strip is cut into 2 parts: 3 cm and 7 cm. Is it cut into halves? Why?
pretest.answer: No. The parts are not equal.

pretest.q: Write 1/2 in the right place on the number line.
How many thirds make one whole?
Which is longer: 1/2 or 1/4 of the same strip?

items.q: Is each part 1/3 of the strip? Write yes or no.
Can you make thirds by folding a strip in half, then in half again? Explain.
items.answer: No. That makes 4 equal parts (quarters), not 3.

items.q: Max's first try at 1/5 of a strip was 4 cm. He stepped it out 5 times and 5 cm was left over. How long is the strip? How long should 1/5 be?
items.answer: The strip is 20 + 5 = 25 cm, so 1/5 is 5 cm.

items.q: What fraction is marked with the dot?
What fraction is marked with the dot?
Ana has walked 2/8 of the track. What fraction of the track is left?
1/4 of a ribbon is 6 cm. How long is the whole ribbon?
Only 0 and 1/3 are labelled. Label where 1 goes.
items.answer: At the last mark, 3 jumps of 1/3 from 0

items.q: Circle the fractions in the eighths family: 3/8, 3/4, 1/8, 8/8, 1/3
Sam says 1/6 is bigger than 1/3 because 6 is bigger than 3. Is he right? Explain.
items.answer: No. Sixths cut the same whole into more parts, so each sixth is shorter. 1/6 < 1/3.

selfCheck: I can make halves, quarters and eighths by halving
I can make thirds and fifths by estimating and adjusting
I can count unit fractions to one whole on a number line
I can find the missing part to make one whole
I can rebuild the whole from a part
I can sort fractions into families and compare unit fractions

rubric.criteria: Making equal parts of a length
rubric.A: Makes thirds and fifths accurately and explains how to adjust any estimate
rubric.B: Makes thirds and fifths by estimate and adjust with few errors
rubric.C: Makes halves, quarters and eighths; thirds and fifths with some help
rubric.D: Makes halves and quarters by folding; parts not always equal
rubric.E: Does not yet make equal parts

rubric.A: Places and names fractions on any line, including past 1, and explains spaces vs marks
rubric.B: Places and names fractions on 0 to 1 lines and writes the whole as a fraction
rubric.C: Places and names halves, quarters and thirds on labelled lines
rubric.D: Places 1/2 on a line; often counts marks not spaces
rubric.E: Does not yet place fractions on a line

rubric.A: Finds missing parts and rebuilds wholes from non-unit fractions (2/3, 3/4)
rubric.B: Finds missing parts and rebuilds wholes from 1/2, 1/4, 1/3 and 1/8
rubric.C: Finds missing parts with strips; rebuilds from 1/2 and 1/4
rubric.D: Finds the missing part for halves only, with help
rubric.E: Does not yet find the missing part

rubric.A: Compares non-unit fractions and explains why equal wholes are needed
rubric.B: Orders unit fractions and explains 'more parts, smaller parts'
rubric.C: Sorts fractions into families and compares 2 unit fractions
rubric.D: Compares unit fractions using a wall, with help
rubric.E: Still thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
